name: avista-dev-machine
description: Get an Avista developer's Mac from nothing to shipping, diagnose-first. A read-only doctor scans base tooling, shell config, gh accounts and token scopes, SSH reachability (which username each host actually greets), the 1Password SSH agent, the agent layer and role tooling, then routes every gap to the skill and step that closes it — most broken machines are half-configured, not fresh, so this usually reduces the job to one or two named fixes. Two setup skills cover everyone: base tooling (Homebrew, git, gh) with a working shell config and per-project gh/SSH account switching, and the agent layer the other Avista plugins assume (Claude Code on PATH, the org marketplace, the shared global instruction file, the ~/.claude/.env token store). Two more are role-scoped and often mutually exclusive: the local WordPress toolchain (PHP with the extensions WordPress needs, Composer, PHPUnit, Node via nvm, Local/Docker + mkcert, the weasyprint+poppler render pair), and SSH access to WPMU DEV client sites. Detect-and-merge rather than clobber: existing configs are backed up and only missing pieces added. Secrets stay with the user — token values are pasted into a 0600 file and never echoed, logged, or passed as process arguments; the token store is inspected by key name; SSH keys come from the 1Password agent and no password or private key is ever handled; production verification is read-only and a changed host key is never auto-cleared.
